sentences.text: This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 20-07-2024, at about 05-15 A.M., the petitioner was proceeding in motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-KK-1463 as a pillion rider.

The said motorcycle was ridden by her son by name Srinivasa who is the petitioner in MVC No. 6344/2024 on the file of this court) on Bettahalli road and when they reached near Bettahalli road,
Saibaba Temple near, Dasanapura Hobli, Bangalore, at that time the driver of the Goods Carrier bearing Reg.no.KA-41-D-4157 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle, result of which she fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Anupama Hospitals, Bangalore wherein admitted as an inpatient for a period of 7 days.

So far,
the petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
She was doing farmer work and earning sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability petitioner is not in a position to do the said work.
She has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of income, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1/the RC owner of Goods Carrier bearing Reg.no.KA-41-D-4157 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex-parte.
5. The respondent No.2 - /the Insurer of Goods Carrier bearing Reg.no.KA-41-D-4157 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of policy subject to its terms and conditions.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident, the petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional police have created false crime records and story as to the occurrence of accident to get compensation and that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license and same was not having RC and permit as on the date of accident.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-KK-1463 as he was not having Driving license and rider and pillion rider not wearing helmet.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that she has sustained injuries on account of road traffic accident on 20-07-2024 at about 5- 15 pm., on Bettahalli road, Saibaba Temple near, Dasanapura Hobli, Bangalore, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Goods Carrier bearing Reg.No.KA-41-D- Jayalakshmi vs Mahesha N C on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161949240/
2. Whether the petitioner proves that she is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What Order or Award?
7. The petitioner got examined herself as Pw1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P10 and closed evidence on petitioner's side.
The respondent no.2 has not adduced any evidence on their behalf.

8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.
9.

,
P.W.1 has filed her affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 20-07-2024, at about 05-15 A.M., when the petitioner was proceeding in motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-KK-1463 as a pillion rider, the said motorcycle was ridden by her son by name Srinivasa who is the petitioner in MVC No. 6344/2024 on the file of this court) on Bettahalli road and when they reached near Bettahalli road, Saibaba Temple near, Dasanapura Hobli, Bangalore, at that time the driver of Goods Carrier bearing Reg.no.KA-41-D-4157 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle, result of which she fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

The P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.,
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to Ex.P6 which are the police records such as FIR with complaint, spot mahazar with photographs of scene of occurrence, wound certificate, notice u/Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply given thereon, IMV report, charge sheet etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Sri Doddabeeriah, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0626/2024 of Madanayakanahally Police Station for the offence punishable under section 125(a), 281 of BNS, 2023.
After completing investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 125(a), 281 of BNS, 2023.

3 13.

During the course of argument it is vehemently argued by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 that since the accident in question has taken place in the middle of the road the rider too has contributed negligence.
Hence, petitioner has to forgo compensation to the percentage of the negligence contributed by the rider of motorcycle.
In order to substantiate the said contention, the learned counsel for respondent no.2 has relied upon the photographs produced along with spot mahazar.
14. It is the contention of the petitioner that the accident in question has occurred while he was proceeding on the left side of the road.
Admittedly, charge sheet is filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.

It is not in dispute that at the time of accident the rider was proceeding towards Bettahalli, whereas the offending vehicle was coming from Bettahalli ie., from opposite direction and there is head on collusion between the two vehicles.
If the spot mahazar is perused, it discloses that the width of the road is nearly 18 feet.
Nowhere in the spot mahazar the spot of accident is identified by describing or narrating the distance from the spot of accident towards left and right edge of the tar road.
Hence, from the spot mahazar court cannot assess the exact spot of accident.
The petitioner has produced the rough eye sketch which discloses the spot of accident is on the extreme left side of Byandahalli - Bettadhahalli road.

As observed supra, the counsel for respondent no.2 has relied upon the photographs of the scene of occurrence wherein one Lakshamanna resident of the said area while drawing mahazar has shown the spot of accident.
If the said document is relied upon there is center line in the road and the place shown by said Lakshmanna is within the center line.
It clearly reveals that the accident in question has occurred in Byandahalli - Bettadhahalli road with in the center line.
When offending vehicle was coming from Bettadhahalli side, he ought to have drive his vehicle within the center line of Bettadhahalli - Byandahalli .

Hence,
it clearly reveals that the driver of the offending vehicle by crossing the center line came towards the right side of Bettadhahalli- Byandahalli road and dashed against the vehicle of the petitioner.
If the driver of the offending vehicle had not crossed the center line and had not come towards the right side of the said road, this accident would not have occurred.
Even though respondent no.2 has contended that the rider has also contributed negligence but they have failed to substantiate the said contention.
The document relied by the respondent no.2 ie., photographs pertaining to the scene of occurrence goes against to the case of the respondent no.2.
The respondents have failed to rebut the contention taken by the petitioner so far as issue no.1 by not adducing the evidence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, materials placed on record clearly proves the rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle in which petitioner has not played any role.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:- P.W.1 has given evidence to the effect of her sustained severe injuries.
Ex.P3 is the wound certificate issued from Anupama Hospital to the effect that petitioner has been treated for five injuries which are grievous in nature.
16. The discharge summary as per Ex.P.7 issued from Anupama Hospital, Bangalore discloses that petitioner has taken treatment from 20-07-2024 to 26- 07-2024.
Thus the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for a period of seven days.
The petitioner has not examined the medical officer who has given treatment to her and there is no evidence on record to say that petitioner has suffered permanent disability.
As such there is no loss of future income.

Hence, petitioner is not Jayalakshmi vs Mahesha N C on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161949240/
4 entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income.

sentences.text: 17. Towards pain and sufferings, the petitioner shown to have sustained five grievous injuries.

Hence taking into consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment etc, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering.
18. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner are concerned, she has produced 17 medical bills for Rs.83,396/- as per Ex.P9.

Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.83,396/-.
19.
It is stated that petitioner was aged about 46years.
She was doing farmer work and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m..
But to substantiate the said contention petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence this court considering the age of petitioner, year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner, taken the income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- p.m.
20.
The petitioner has sustained five grievous injuries and has taken treatment for 7 days as inpatient at Anupama Hospital.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, which are grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 2 months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking into consideration the avocation of petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation, this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.16,500/- p.m. for two month.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.33,000/- towards loss of income during the laid down period .
21.
From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient at Anupama Hospital.
Further for taking treatment as inpatient in the said hospital she was traveled to hospital for treatment.
She has taken nourishment and needs further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.25,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2024.
22. The petitioner at her age of 46 years has suffered grievous injuries which definitely caused some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort to the tune of Rs.60,000/-.

Thus the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.
 1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 70,000/-
 2. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 25,000/-
 charges and nourishing food  & other incidental charges

3 . Medical expenses Rs. 83,396/-
 4. Loss of income during laid down Rs. 33,000/-
 period  5. Loss of discomfort and amenities Rs. 60,000/-
Jayalakshmi vs Mahesha N C on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161949240/
5  Total Rs. 2,71,396/-
Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,71,396/- (Rupees Two Lakh Seventy One Thousand Three Hundred Ninety Six only)
23.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
24. Issue No.3:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.2,71,396/- + cost of Rs.1,000/- imposed vide order on IA No. I & II.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.2,72,396/- (Rupees Two Lakh Seventy Two Thousand Three Hundred Ninety Six only).
A Sum of Rs.2,71,396/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in her name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 2nd day of September 2025.)
(ROOPASHRI) XXII Addl. SCJ & ACJM Bengaluru.
